source.title_on_document: The effects of generative AI model type and visual stimuli type on design creativity

paper_design_summary: A controlled between-groups study involved 84 environmental-design students divided equally among four conditions crossing ChatGPT-4o text-to-image versus Midjourney image-to-image assistance with figurative versus abstract visual stimuli; groups were balanced by year, but random assignment is not stated (p. 3, Methods; pp. 4–5, Materials). Participants generated exhibition-design ideas and then refined a proposal by hand-drawing; eight experts rated the ideas and final designs for creativity-related dimensions, including originality and reliance on AI image features (pp. 5–6, Experimental procedure and Creativity assessment).

studies.label: AI model type and visual stimuli in exhibition design

assignment.what_was_assigned: Participants were divided among conditions crossing generative-AI image-generation modality (text-to-image ChatGPT-4o versus image-to-image Midjourney) and visual stimulus type (figurative versus abstract). Equal division and balance by study year are stated, but the allocation mechanism beyond that is not described (p. 3, Participants and Experimental design; p. 4, Materials).
assignment.quote: Participants were then divided equally into four groups, ensuring that the number of second- and third-year students within each group was within the range of 10–11.

arms.name: T2I AI + figurative visual stimuli
arms.description: ChatGPT-4o with figurative visual reference images. One of the equally divided groups described on p. 3; an arm-specific analyzed count is not printed (pp. 3–5, Methods).

arms.name: T2I AI + abstract visual stimuli
arms.description: ChatGPT-4o with abstract visual reference images. One of the equally divided groups described on p. 3; an arm-specific analyzed count is not printed (pp. 3–5, Methods).

arms.name: I2I AI + figurative visual stimuli
arms.description: Midjourney with figurative visual reference images. One of the equally divided groups described on p. 3; an arm-specific analyzed count is not printed (pp. 3–5, Methods).

arms.name: I2I AI + abstract visual stimuli
arms.description: Midjourney with abstract visual reference images. One of the equally divided groups described on p. 3; an arm-specific analyzed count is not printed (pp. 3–5, Methods).

participants.exclusions: Not stated. The reported study sample is not accompanied by exclusion accounting, a separate analytic N, or per-arm analyzed counts (p. 3, Participants; pp. 6-8, Results and Tables 1-2).
participants.who: University students majoring in environmental design, comprising sophomores and juniors, without prior in-depth exposure to generative AI-assisted design. The reported study sample is 84; a separate post-exclusion analytic count is not stated. The assessment describes scoring the solutions provided by each participant.
participants.quote: A total of 84 university students took part in this study, with a male-to-female ratio of nearly 1:1 and an average age of 21 ± 0.92 years.
participants.locator: p. 3, Methods — Participants (reported study sample); pp. 5–6, Creativity assessment (participant submissions scored)

ai_tool.name_model: ChatGPT-4o (text-to-image) and Midjourney (image-to-image; version not stated)
ai_tool.how_used: Participants used the assigned AI tool and supplied visual reference materials to generate inspirational images for their own design ideas. The paper identifies ChatGPT-4o as the text-to-image condition and Midjourney as the image-to-image condition (pp. 4–5, Materials and Experimental procedure).

task.description: Develop an overseas Terracotta Warriors exhibition that conveys a vast army using a single pair of warrior and horse statues. Generate multiple ideas using graphics, phrases or keywords, then hand-draw one refined proposal with a theme, sketch and description (p. 5, Experimental procedure).
task.duration: 60 min total: 5 min instructions, 30 min initial ideation, and 25 min proposal refinement (p. 5, Experimental procedure).

outcomes.name: Originality of initial design ideas (divergent phase)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Eight independent experts scored each participant's submissions on a 1–7 scale; the final dimension score is the average of the eight experts' scores (p. 6, Creativity assessment). The coded unit is the participant submission score, not an individual expert rating. Originality assesses the novelty, uniqueness, and problem-solving originality of initial design concepts (pp. 3 and 5, Experimental design and Creativity assessment). Task 1 explicitly uses the assigned AI tool while generating these ideas (p. 5, Experimental procedure).

outcomes.name: Repetition of AI-generated image features (design fixation; divergent phase)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Eight independent experts scored each participant's submissions on a 1–7 scale; the final dimension score is the average of the eight experts' scores (p. 6, Creativity assessment). The coded unit is the participant submission score, not an individual expert rating. Experts compare participants' sketches with the AI-generated images they used. Repetition measures reliance on those image features; a higher score indicates greater design fixation and lower creative independence (p. 3, Experimental design; p. 5, Creativity assessment). This does not measure similarity across different people. Task 1 explicitly uses AI (p. 5, Experimental procedure).

contrasts.treatment_arm: T2I AI (ChatGPT-4o), pooled across figurative and abstract visual-stimulus conditions
contrasts.control_arm: I2I AI (Midjourney), pooled across figurative and abstract visual-stimulus conditions
contrasts.reported: T2I AI vs. I2I AI, across visual-stimulus conditions: 3.84 ± 0.148 vs. 3.003 ± 0.148, p < 0.001. AI-type main effect: F = 15.456, p ≤ 0.001, η²p = 0.162. The prose does not label the ± quantities as SD or SE. Higher scores indicate greater reliance on the participant’s AI-generated images; this is not similarity across different people’s outputs. η²p is the reported partial eta-squared, not a standardized mean difference. The structured direction describes the raw repetition score; the higher score is detrimental, not a creativity benefit.

eligibility.reason: The paper states equal division into groups balanced by study year, without stating random assignment or an explicitly non-random allocation mechanism (p. 3, Participants). Criterion 1 is therefore unclear; design_class remains other and no observational context classification is established. The paper reports 84 students who took part, but no separate analyzed N, exclusion accounting, or per-arm analyzed counts (p. 3, Participants; pp. 6-8, Results and Tables 1-2). Under the form rule that criterion 2 counts people analyzed, the threshold is unclear, not confirmed as met or not met. Criterion 3 is met because experts scored participants' produced ideas and refined proposals (pp. 5-6, Creativity assessment). Core eligibility remains unclear. All conditions involve generative AI and compare AI configurations; repetition measures dependence on AI exemplars rather than diversity across people (pp. 3-5, Methods).

one_line_finding: Text-to-image ChatGPT-4o users scored higher than image-to-image Midjourney users on divergent originality (3.685 vs. 2.813, p < 0.001) and repetition of AI image features (3.84 vs. 3.003, p < 0.001), indicating greater design fixation (p. 6, Results — The impact of generative AI on design creativity).
open_questions: Was allocation to the four conditions randomized? Equal division and study-year balance alone do not specify the mechanism (p. 3, Participants).

How many participants entered each analysis and each arm? The paper reports 84 students taking part without a separate analytic N or exclusion accounting (p. 3, Participants; pp. 6-8, Results and Tables 1-2).
Was the AI tool available during Task 2 hand-drawn refinement? Availability and removal are not explicit; the convergent with_ai question code is provisional (p. 5, Experimental procedure).
Which AI-type main-effect statistics are correct for convergent abstractness and aesthetic appeal? The p. 6 prose and p. 7 Table 1 conflict; the form retains both and selects no adjudicated value.
notes: The complete local markdown conversion was read through the references; no appendix or supplementary file is identified. All eleven scored dimensions are listed and the recorded numbers were checked in the PDF. Convergent AI availability is null because the document does not explicitly state availability or removal during hand-drawing; mixed would assert a pattern that is also not reported. The with_ai labels for those outcomes are provisional, not evidence of a confirmed after_ai condition. For divergent fluency and flexibility, the means are expert-assigned scores on the 1–7 scale, not raw idea/category counts (pp. 5-6). The standardized_effect flags refer only to reported partial eta-squared (η²p), not standardized mean differences. No effect size was calculated. For the separate convergent simple comparisons, p_value_only describes the inferential information; Table 2 also supplies means and labeled SDs but no analyzed arm Ns, so arm_means_sds_ns is not marked (p. 8). Higher repetition indicates more fixation; treatment_higher records its raw score direction and is not a creativity benefit (pp. 3 and 6). Conflicting convergent abstractness and aesthetic-appeal main effects are reported with both source locations and no adjudicated value (pp. 6-7).

applied.old: Only divergent originality and repetition are listed; divergent fluency, flexibility, and practicality are missing.
applied.new: Added S1-O4 divergent fluency, S1-O5 divergent flexibility, and S1-O6 divergent practicality, including the verified marginal scores and AI-type F, p, and partial eta-squared values. Fluency and flexibility are identified as count-based scores on the 1–7 scale, not raw counts.
applied.quote: Judges rated the submissions across five dimensions: originality (novelty), fluency (number of ideas generated), flexibility (diversity of perspectives), practicality (feasibility of the preliminary idea), and repetition (degree of reliance on AI exemplars).
applied.locator: PDF p. 3, Experimental design; pp. 5–6, Creativity assessment; p. 6, The impact of generative AI on design creativity; p. 7, Table 1.

applied.old: Only convergent originality is listed; elaboration, flexibility, abstractness, aesthetic appeal, and contextual adaptability are missing.
applied.new: Added S1-O7 elaboration, S1-O8 flexibility, S1-O9 abstractness, S1-O10 aesthetic appeal, and S1-O11 contextual adaptability for the convergent phase. Both conflicting p. 6 prose and p. 7 Table 1 main-effect entries are retained for abstractness and aesthetic appeal; adjudicated values are null. Separate figurative-stimulus Table 2 comparisons and abstract-stimulus p-value comparisons were added to all six convergent outcomes, including S1-O2, without conflating them with the main effects. Source conflicts are recorded in notes and open_questions.
applied.quote: The creativity of the refined design proposals is measured from six dimensions: originality, elaboration, flexibility, abstractness, aesthetic appeal, and contextual adaptability.
applied.locator: PDF pp. 3–4, Experimental design; pp. 5–6, Creativity assessment; p. 6, The impact of generative AI on design creativity; p. 7, Table 1; p. 8, Table 2.

applied.old: All three measure_detail strings are empty.
applied.new: All eleven measure_detail fields now describe the eight independent experts, 1–7 scale, averaging of expert scores, and each construct. Originality is novelty of the participant's design; repetition is dependence on that participant's AI-generated images.
applied.quote: To ensure reliability, the final score for each dimension was the average of the eight experts’ scores.
applied.locator: PDF pp. 5–6, Creativity assessment; p. 3, Experimental design (repetition definition).

applied.old: For all three recorded contrasts, the arm labels, comparison_type, and direction are empty strings and statistics_available is [].
applied.new: For every AI-type main contrast, treatment_arm = T2I AI (ChatGPT-4o), pooled across visual-stimulus conditions; control_arm = I2I AI (Midjourney), pooled across visual-stimulus conditions; comparison_type = ai_design; direction = treatment_higher; statistics_available = [test_statistic, standardized_effect]. Partial eta-squared is named explicitly and no arm_means_sds_ns flag is used. Higher repetition is identified as more fixation, not a creativity benefit.
applied.quote: Compared to those using the I2I AI model, participants using the T2I AI model present better results in design creativity, but they are also more likely to experience design fixation.
applied.locator: PDF p. 4, Materials; p. 6, The impact of generative AI on design creativity; p. 7, Table 1; p. 9, first Discussion subsection (convergent direction).

applied.old: All three timing strings are empty.
applied.new: timing = immediate for all eleven outcomes, produced during the same 60 min session: 5 min instructions, 30 min Task 1, and 25 min Task 2 (p. 5, Experimental procedure).
applied.quote: The experiment lasted 60 min (see Figure 3), and the procedure is outlined below.

applied.old: Both divergent-phase ai_available_when_produced strings are empty.
applied.new: ai_available_when_produced = yes for S1-O1 and S1-O3 and all three added divergent outcomes. For all six convergent outcomes it is null because Task 2 does not explicitly state continued availability or removal. The uncertainty and provisional with_ai coding are described in measure_detail, notes, and open_questions; no after_ai condition is asserted.
applied.quote: Each group received two different reference images, and worked with different AI-based tools to generate images to provide as many design ideas and solutions as possible through graphics, phrases, or keywords.
applied.locator: PDF p. 5, Experimental procedure, Task 1 and Task 2; p. 3, Experimental design.
